record_type_quote: In the current study, we conducted a preregistered direct and conceptual replication of this previous research using a large nationally representative sample.

targets.authors: Toner, K., Leary, M. R., Asher, M. W., & Jongman-Sereno, K. P.
targets.title: Feeling superior is a bipartisan issue: Extremity (not direction) of political views predicts perceived belief superiority.
targets.evidence_quote: We sought to directly and conceptually replicate Toner et al.’s (2013) finding regarding dogmatism.
targets.outcome_quote: Consistent with Toner et al.’s findings, our results showed that conservatives had higher dogmatism scores than liberals, whereas both conservative and liberal extreme attitudes were associated with higher belief superiority compared with more moderate attitudes. As in their study, we also found that whether conservative or liberal attitudes were associated with higher belief superiority was topic dependent. Contrasting Toner et al.’s findings, our results also showed that ideologically extreme individuals had higher dogmatism.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors confirm belief superiority and linear dogmatism comparisons but explicitly contrast the curvilinear dogmatism result. Statements that particular relationships successfully replicated do not give an overall verdict that overrides this contrast.
